In [[mathematics]], two [[non-empty]] [[subset]]s ''A'' and ''B'' of a given [[metric space]] (''X'',&nbsp;''d'') are said to be '''positively separated''' if the [[infimum]]

:<math>\inf_{a \in A, b \in B} d(a, b) > 0.</math>
 
(Some authors also specify that ''A'' and ''B'' should be [[disjoint sets]]; however, this adds nothing to the definition, since if ''A'' and ''B'' have some common point ''p'', then ''d''(''p'',&nbsp;''p'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;0, and so the infimum above is clearly 0 in that case.)

For example, on the real line with the usual distance, the [[open interval]]s (0,&nbsp;2) and (3,&nbsp;4) are positively separated, while (3,&nbsp;4) and (4,&nbsp;5) are not. In two dimensions, the graph of ''y''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1/''x'' for ''x''&nbsp;&gt;&nbsp;0 and the ''x''-axis are not positively separated.
